clue.text: Bad sign in second variety of citrus fruit

parts.note: bad means evil
Leo is a sign of the zodiac
a range is a variety, as in a wide range of goods

explanation.surface: Some dreadful omen is found in a lesser sort of lemon or lime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' only joins the pieces here. The Seville orange is the bitter orange used for marmalade.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bitter orange grown around the Spanish city, the classic fruit for marmalade.

clue.text: Weaken the force of degree with English, securing university diploma finally

indicators.note: securing means holding something firmly inside, so the other letters go within

parts.note: extent means degree, as in to some extent

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word diploma

explanation.surface: A graduate's qualification is downplayed, with an English degree secured only after the diploma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' wraps the degree-plus-English string around the university letter and the last letter of 'diploma'; 'with' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To extenuate an offence is to lessen its seriousness by offering excuses.

clue.text: Run in, enthusiastic about opening

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: into means keen on, as in being really into jazz
R is the cricket scoreboard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A keen runner is eager to get going at the start of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link. INTO, informal for keen on, goes 'about' R to make IN-R-TO.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section of a song or piece.

clue.text: A cry I'll put out, being so expressive

indicators.note: put out suggests the letters are disturbed and set out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone lets out a heartfelt cry, the very picture of emotional expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges the letters of A CRY I'LL; 'being so' links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyrical writing or speech is warmly and poetically expressive of feeling.

clue.text: It's left, not right as planned, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: odd means not right, strange, and meant means planned, so together they make odd meant

explanation.surface: Something went awry with the plan, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns ODD MEANT into a word sounding the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover piece, a remnant remaining once the rest has gone.

clue.text: Short of power at first, fastidious about joints

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so one letter is taken away
at first places the dropped letter at the front of the word

parts.note: particular means fastidious, fussy about details
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A fussy person, lacking energy at the start, worries about stiff joints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' and 'at first' together drop the opening P from PARTICULAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Articular is an anatomical adjective meaning relating to the body's joints.

clue.text: Sound of pain increased in volume, audibly

indicators.note: audibly signals that the word is to be judged by its spoken sound

parts.note: grown means increased in size or volume

explanation.surface: A cry of agony grows louder and louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' turns GROWN into a word that sounds identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a low moan uttered by someone hurting.

clue.text: Shared concern?

parts.note: a worry held in common is the surface, but a concern is a business and shared means divided into shares traded on a stock exchange

explanation.definitionFit: A firm whose shares are offered for sale on the open market to anyone.

clue.text: Awkwardness being excused?

parts.note: being excused is the polite phrase for going to the toilet, and a public lavatory is a convenience, so someone excused is in one

explanation.walkthrough: Split as IN CONVENIENCE: British English calls a public toilet a convenience.
explanation.definitionFit: Inconvenience means trouble or awkwardness caused to someone.

clue.text: Frisky, turned out in raw

indicators.note: frisky means lively and playful, so these letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: A lively young recruit turns out to be very green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisky' rearranges the letters of TURNED OUT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw in the sense of inexperienced: someone untrained, never taught.

clue.text: Ancient character of type of tree

definitions.meaning: a letter of the old runic and Old English alphabet, standing for th
a hawthorn or similar prickly shrub or tree

explanation.surface: An old personality is said to be a certain kind of tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: an Old English letter and a spiny bush such as hawthorn.

clue.text: Speech in Klingon?

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the single word Klingon

explanation.surface: A fan wonders about talk in the alien language from Star Trek.
explanation.walkthrough: Klingon is the invented alien language from Star Trek, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for language, a particular way of speaking.

clue.text: No end to street party's increasing intensity

indicators.note: no end to means the final letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a crescent is a curved street
a do is a party; the 's is is

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood street party gets louder and louder, with no end in sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A crescent is a curved British street; 'No end to' removes its final letter before the party word joins on.
explanation.definitionFit: In music a crescendo is a gradual rise in loudness.

clue.text: Part of the church using casual Latin

parts.note: chance as an adjective means casual, accidental, as in a chance meeting

explanation.surface: The clergy use relaxed Latin in a section of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual' is not an anagram signal here; it is a synonym for the adjective chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area around the altar, reserved for clergy and choir.

clue.text: Vessel is able to, crossing a river

indicators.note: crossing means stretching over, so one piece is set around the other

parts.note: can means is able to
the Tamar is the river dividing Devon from Cornwall in England

explanation.surface: A boat can manage to get across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tamar is the river forming most of the border between Devon and Cornwall; 'crossing' means the 'is able to' word spans it.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamaran is a boat with two parallel hulls.

clue.text: City's examination licence retracted

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: a viva is an oral examination
let means permission or licence, as in without let or hindrance

explanation.surface: Someone's driving test pass and permit are withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retracted' reads VIVA plus LET backwards as one string, making the Israeli city; 'City's' is City is.
explanation.definitionFit: Tel Aviv is the major Mediterranean city of Israel.

clue.text: Card that might help to win a hand

definitions.text: Card that might help to win a hand

parts.words: Card that might help to win a hand
parts.note: a hand suggests card games, but here it is a hand in marriage, won by a romantic card sent in February

explanation.definitionFit: A card sent anonymously on 14 February to someone you are sweet on.

clue.text: The briefest dance?

parts.note: a dance consisting of a single pace would be about as brief as dancing gets; the name of an early ballroom dance says just that

explanation.definitionFit: A quick ballroom dance in duple time, popular in the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Deeply thinking writers I have to follow

indicators.note: to follow tells us the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: pens are writing implements, things that write
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Authors I admire to follow are thoughtful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensive means lost in serious thought, reflective.

clue.text: Girl in mini, perhaps, with short legwear turned over

parts.note: the Mini is a small car, given as an example

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the letters run backwards
short means a letter is cut off the end

parts.note: nylons are stockings, so nylon stands for legwear

explanation.surface: A young woman in a miniskirt, perhaps, with hosiery pulled up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mini' suggests a skirt but is the car. 'short' cuts NYLON to NYLO, and 'turned over' makes OLYN.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolyn is a female first name.

clue.text: Framework which assistant can divulge

indicators.note: can divulge means the run of words reveals letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: Which assistant can spill the beans about the structure?
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a vehicle or appliance.

clue.text: Pray madly about love with guy, one showing burning desire

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the others
madly means wildly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
a guy is a man
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone prays wildly about their love for a man, revealing passionate yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' turns PRAY into PYRA, which goes 'about' O, MAN and I; 'with' and 'one showing' link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pyromania is a compulsion to set fires, literally a craving for burning.

clue.text: Frenetically chart progress in stages

indicators.note: frenetically means in a wild frenzy, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone frantically maps the advance step by step.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratch is a variant of ratchet, to move forward notch by notch.

clue.text: Adrift once, without a thing to paddle

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the shuffled letters surround the other piece
adrift means floating loose, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Once lost at sea, without a means to row ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: a rearrangement of ONCE goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light narrow boat propelled with a paddle.

clue.text: Arrived with nothing to make brief appearance

parts.note: came means arrived
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A star turned up with nothing to do but pop in briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small part played by a famous actor.

clue.text: One keeps records, going back about a century

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a ton is a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: An archivist's files stretch back about a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' turns RE plus TON into a single backwards run.
explanation.definitionFit: A noter is someone who writes things down, a recorder.

clue.text: Unable to settle down for retirement?

definitions.text: Unable to settle down for retirement?

parts.words: Unable to settle down for retirement?
parts.note: retirement suggests leaving work, but here it means going to bed, so the person cannot get to sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who habitually cannot sleep.

clue.text: Manifest in Zeus's sudden downfall

indicators.note: in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: the Thunderer is a title of Zeus, god of thunder; the 's adds no letter
to manifest is to show

explanation.surface: A display appears in the sudden fall of the king of the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: Zeus, like Jupiter, is called the Thunderer as god of thunder; 'in' sets the display word inside that title, and 'downfall' is a fall of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief heavy rainstorm with thunder, literally a downpour that comes suddenly.
